Welcome to Edward Pauling Primary School
It is my pleasure to warmly welcome you to Edward Pauling Primary School, a place where every child is valued, inspired, and supported to reach their full potential.
As Headteacher, I am proud to lead a team committed to fostering a positive, inclusive, and nurturing environment grounded in our core values. One of my core priorities is to support our dedicated staff, who work tirelessly, to deliver high-quality teaching that sparks curiosity, creativity, and resilience in every child.
Our values underpin everything we do, encouraging our children to be resilient, empathetic, respectful, independent, ambitious, and courageous in their learning journey preparing them for life beyond Edward Pauling.
We believe that learning extends beyond the classroom, and we prioritise personal development and well-being alongside academic progress. Here, children grow not only as learners but as confident, respectful individuals who demonstrate empathy and independence, ready to embrace the future with courage and ambition.
We value constructive feedback and continuously strive to enhance the quality of education and the overall experience for our children and families. I invite you to explore our website to discover more about our vision, values, and the vibrant life within our school community.
Together, we can ensure every child thrives.
Adam Malin- Headteacher

Vision and Values
We are: Kind, Resilient, Ambitious
Our core values—Resilient, Empathetic, Respectful, Independent, Courageous, and Ambitious—are not just words; they are lived every day through the actions and attitudes of our children, staff, and wider school community.
Resilient: We encourage children to embrace challenges and learn from setbacks. For example, when faced with difficult tasks, children are supported to keep trying, knowing that perseverance leads to success. Our staff model resilience by maintaining a calm and positive approach, helping children to develop emotional regulation and bounce back from difficulties.
Empathetic: Our school community values kindness and understanding. Children are taught to listen to others’ perspectives and offer support when someone is upset or struggling. Activities such as peer mentoring and circle time discussions help children develop empathy and build strong, supportive friendships.
Respectful: Respect is shown in how we treat each other and our environment. Children are expected to use polite language, listen when others are speaking, and care for school property. Staff and children alike demonstrate respect by valuing diverse opinions and celebrating individual differences, creating an inclusive atmosphere where everyone feels valued.
Independent: We foster independence by encouraging children to take responsibility for their learning and behaviour. For example, children are taught to organise their own resources, make choices about their learning activities, and reflect on their behaviour through restorative conversations. This prepares them to be self-motivated learners.
Courageous: Trying new things and stepping out of comfort zones is celebrated. Whether it’s participating in a new sport, speaking in front of the class, or admitting when they need help, children are supported to show bravery and take positive risks in their learning and personal growth.
Ambitious: We set high expectations for all children, encouraging them to aim high and achieve their best. Our curriculum is designed to challenge and inspire, and we celebrate achievements both big and small. Children are encouraged to set personal goals and reflect on their progress regularly.
These values are embedded in daily routines, lessons, and interactions, helping to create a calm, safe, and supportive environment where positive behaviour is the norm. Through consistent reinforcement and modelling by all staff, children internalise these values and understand how their behaviour impacts themselves and others. This shared commitment helps us build a strong, respectful school culture where every child can thrive.

PSHE (including RSE)
At Edward Pauling Primary School, we believe every child deserves an education that prepares them not only for academic success but also to thrive as rounded individuals in modern society. Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education sits at the heart of this commitment.
PSHE is not an add-on to our curriculum; it is fundamental to our children’s development as confident, healthy and respectful members of society. Through high-quality PSHE, we equip pupils with the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to stay safe, maintain wellbeing, and build positive relationships throughout their lives.
Our curriculum is carefully designed to be developmental and progressive. From the moment children join our school, they begin to explore emotional literacy—learning to recognise, name and talk about feelings. This foundation grows year by year, helping pupils to manage emotions, develop resilience, and make informed decisions that support their own and others’ wellbeing.
By embedding PSHE across our school culture, we nurture a community where respect, inclusivity and responsibility flourish. In doing so, we prepare our pupils not only for the challenges of childhood but also for adulthood, work and active citizenship.
We are committed to:
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE) is our comprehensive curriculum for supporting children's personal development, health, wellbeing and understanding of relationships.
Parent Engagement and the Right to Withdraw
We are required by law to teach Relationships Education and Health Education to all primary-aged pupils. We deliver these statutory subjects within our broader PSHE programme. Where we teach about human reproduction (sex education), we do so in line with the principles and approach of the 2025 Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) statutory guidance, in which sex education itself remains non-statutory (but recommended) in primary schools.
Relationships Education is compulsory for all primary-aged children and there is no right of withdrawal. It focuses on teaching children the fundamental building blocks of positive, respectful relationships with family, friends, peers and adults.
Health Education is compulsory for all primary-aged children and there is no right of withdrawal. It focuses on supporting children to make informed decisions about their health and wellbeing.
Sex education is not compulsory in primary schools, however the Department for Education recommends that all primary schools teach age-appropriate sex education to ensure children are prepared for the changes adolescence brings and understand how human life begins.
The following Jigsaw lessons in the Changing Me Puzzle contain non-statutory sex education content:
Year 6: Babies: Conception to Birth
Parents have the right to request that their child be withdrawn from some or all of sex education taught as part of PSHE. Parents do NOT have the right to withdraw children from:
Before making a decision to withdraw a child from sex education, we invite parents to discuss their concerns with the Headteacher. This discussion helps us to understand the request and enables us to clarify the nature and purpose of the curriculum, discuss the benefits of the education, and consider any potential impacts of withdrawal on the child.
Where a parent requests withdrawal, we will:
We inform parents about sex education content by sending curriculum information letters at the start of the summer term and holding a parent information session where we share all teaching materials.
A withdrawal request form is available from the school office and on our website in our RSE Policy.
Our PSHE curriculum also includes age-appropriate aspects of economic education, preparing children to understand spending, saving and the world of work, and citizenship education including British Values, helping children understand their rights, responsibilities and role in society.
We take a whole-school approach to PSHE education and how we meet our statutory duties.
Under the Education Act 2002 and the Academies Act 2010, all schools must provide a curriculum that:
• Promotes the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils
• Prepares pupils for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of later life
The Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education (England) Regulations (updated July 2025) make Relationships Education and Health Education statutory for all primary-aged pupils. These subjects must be taught in all maintained schools, academies, independent schools, maintained special schools, non-maintained special schools, and alternative provision settings.
We deliver statutory Relationships and Health Education within our comprehensive PSHE programme, using materials from Jigsaw PSHE 3-11. This provides children with a carefully sequenced, age-appropriate curriculum that meets all statutory requirements whilst also developing wider personal and social capabilities. Our PSHE curriculum also supports our safeguarding responsibilities as set out in Keeping Children Safe in Education and the Prevent Duty, helping children to recognise concerns, stay safe online and offline, and seek help when needed.
Our curriculum addresses all statutory requirements including:
• Families and people who care for me
• Caring friendships
• Respectful, kind relationships
• Online safety and awareness
• Internet safety and harms
• Physical health and fitness
• Drugs, alcohol, tobacco and vaping
• Health protection and prevention
• Developing bodies (including puberty as part of Health Education)
A detailed mapping document showing how the Jigsaw programme covers every statutory outcome is available to view on request and is shared via email each half term prior to teaching. In the Summer Term we hold parental workshops in Year 5 and 6 to share teaching resources prior to teaching the Changing Me Puzzle.

Maths
At our school, Maths develops children’s fluency, mathematical thinking and problem-solving skills, giving every pupil the confidence to become a successful mathematician. We believe that all children can achieve in mathematics and provide opportunities for pupils to develop a deep and lasting understanding of mathematical concepts. Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that children build on prior learning, make connections between ideas and develop secure conceptual understanding. Through a focus on number sense, place value, calculation, fractions, geometry, measurement and statistics, pupils develop a strong mathematical foundation. Children are encouraged to reason, explain their thinking, make connections and solve problems in a range of contexts. They use mathematical vocabulary accurately and learn to represent their thinking using concrete resources, pictorial representations and abstract methods. Pupils are supported to explore different strategies, identify patterns and articulate why a method works, rather than simply learning procedures by rote. We place a strong emphasis on fluency, reasoning and problem solving, with children given opportunities to apply their knowledge to increasingly challenging and unfamiliar situations. Through discussion, collaboration and a positive attitude towards mistakes, pupils develop resilience, independence and a growth mindset, learning to see themselves as confident and capable mathematicians.

Music
At Edward Pauling Primary School, Music gives every child the opportunity to discover, create and enjoy music. Through a rich and varied curriculum, pupils develop their musical knowledge, confidence and creativity, while experiencing music from different cultures, traditions and periods. Children learn to sing and perform, listen and respond, compose and improvise, developing their understanding of rhythm, pulse, melody, pitch, dynamics and notation. They explore a range of instruments and learn to play both individually and as part of an ensemble, developing their ability to listen carefully, perform with others and express themselves musically. Our pupils are encouraged to experiment with sounds, create and refine their own musical ideas and respond thoughtfully to the music they hear. Through regular opportunities to perform and share their work, children develop confidence, collaboration, creativity and a lifelong appreciation and enjoyment of music.

Science
At Edward Pauling Primary School, science inspires children to be curious about the world around them and to develop the knowledge and skills needed to think and work like scientists. Through a carefully sequenced curriculum, pupils build a secure understanding of key scientific concepts while developing their ability to question, investigate, observe and explain. Children develop their scientific knowledge and vocabulary across areas including plants, animals, materials, forces, energy, Earth and space, living things and their environments. They make connections between different areas of science and build on prior learning, developing a deeper understanding of the world around them. Our pupils develop essential working scientifically skills, including asking questions, making predictions, planning and carrying out investigations, observing and measuring, recording and presenting results, identifying patterns, drawing conclusions and evaluating evidence. They learn to use equipment safely and appropriately and to communicate their findings using scientific language. We encourage children to think critically, challenge ideas and use evidence to support their conclusions. Through practical investigations and real-world contexts, pupils develop curiosity, resilience, collaboration and problem-solving skills, while learning about the role science plays in our everyday lives and the wider world.

Curriculum Overview
At Edward Pauling Primary School we aim to provide a broad and balanced curriculum that meets the needs of all pupils. Pupils in Years 1-6 follow the National Curriculum which is available online at: https://www.gov.uk/national-curriculum
We have developed our Long Term Plan which ensures that all National Curriculum objectives are met and are taught in an engaging way.
At Edward Pauling Primary School, all pupils from Nursery through to Year 6 learn through a core text, as part of the Power of Reading Programme, details of which can be found at https://www.clpe.org.uk/powerofreading
The core text is at the centre of all lessons and links subjects together to ensure consistency and cohesion. Please see below for the whole school Long Term Plan.
Our daily Guided Reading takes place across Year 1 to Year 6. Guided Reading is taught via a progressive approach based on recalling, deducing, inferring and interpretation skills through a range of genres and text types, using both Power of Reading texts and the Cracking Comprehension scheme. Find out more information at https://www.risingstars-uk.com/subjects/english/cracking-comprehension . Our parent volunteers come into school to support our pupils with their reading development by hearing individual readers and small guided groups on a weekly basis. We follow the Oxford Reading Tree reading scheme for our pupils' independent reading.
Discrete teaching of phonics takes place throughout the Foundation Stage and Key Stage 1, following the RWInc scheme (www.ruthmiskin.com). Additionally, phonics skills are applied by pupils through daily literacy lessons and across the wider curriculum.
Writing skills including vocabulary, grammar and punctuation are taught daily throughout discrete English lessons, as well as through Science and Humanities lessons. Pupils are assessed on their progress in writing by completing sustained writes linked to the learning across subjects. The school has its own spelling programme designed to follow the requirements of the National Curriculum: pupils learn spellings each week and these are also used as part of teaching handwriting to give additional opportunities to embed this learning.
Mathematics is taught daily both in discrete lessons and by applying mathematics skills across the curriculum. Our maths programme ensures full coverage of all the curriculum objectives as well as challenging all pupils to achieve their best through extending understanding of mathematical concepts and the opportunity to develop critical thinking skills. As developing fluency in mental mathematics forms an important part of the curriculum to build pupils' confidence, pupils participate in daily starter activities built around the learning and application of number facts within different contexts.
The planning and implementation of Science is in line with the National Curriculum statutory requirements. Each year group has individualised long, medium and short term planning which is adapted where necessary to meet the learners' needs. Pupils are given opportunities to offer ideas to carry out investigations, set out fair tests, observe, draw conclusions and also develop their research skills.
The school's curriculum for foundation subjects includes Computing, History, Geography, Art and Design, DT (Design Technology), Music and PSHE and provides opportunities for pupils to use their reading, writing, mathematical and communication skills through a wide range of learning opportunities. In addition to the National Curriculum the school is also required to teach RE (Religious Education) which is informed by the Hounslow RE Syllabus. Key Stage 2 pupils also learn Spanish in weekly lessons.
Computing at our school is taught via Purple Mash which has been written to match the National Curriculum aims for Computing (https://www.2simple.com/purple-mash/). It enables computing to be taught as a discrete lesson following a progressive scheme of work for Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2. Computing skills are also applied across the wider curriculum through Science, Humanities, English and Mathematics lessons.
Within Art and Design, pupils have the opportunity to explore and acquire a variety of techniques such as drawing and painting, collage, textile, 3D design, printmaking and digital media through discrete lessons following a progressive scheme of work for Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 linked to key artists. The work in Art and Design is woven into the wider curriculum where pupils can make links with different subjects. Alongside this, Design and Technology is taught at our school by providing a broad and balanced programme where pupils participate in learning experiences involving structures, mechanisms, food technology, materials and textiles.
Music is taught in a variety of ways by utilising cross curricular links with other subjects. We use the Charanga scheme of work which provides teachers with a basis on which they can develop their lessons, ensuring all pupils receive clear lessons from confident and prepared staff. Charanga offers all pupils the chance to participate in a range of music activities, so as to make learning fun and more accessible for all pupils involved. We utilise this scheme of work across the Key Stages, starting in Year 1 and continuing to Year 6.
You can find out more about Charanga at https://charanga.com/site/
We have specialist teachers for PE and have a wide range of extra-curricular clubs. The PE Team engage with outside specialist providers, including those offering competitive sport, and Sport Impact to ensure that all groups of pupils have opportunities to attend competitions. We are proud of our varied extra-curricular programme including sports such as netball, cricket, football, running and badminton for Key Stage 2 and football and multi skills for Key Stage 1. Non-sporting clubs include enrichment, henna, sewing and art. We have been able to offer all pupils the opportunity to attend at least one club and have used funding to ensure that barriers for disadvantaged pupils attending are removed.

Art & Design
At Edward Pauling Primary School, Art and Design inspires children to be creative, curious and confident. Through a progressive curriculum, pupils develop their artistic skills, knowledge and understanding while discovering that there are many different ways to express ideas and respond to the world around them. Children use sketchbooks as a personal space to explore, experiment and develop ideas, recording observations, trying out different techniques and revisiting their work. They take inspiration from a diverse range of artists, craftspeople and designers and use what they discover to inform their own creative responses. Our pupils develop a broad range of making skills, including drawing, painting and mixed media, sculpture and 3D, craft and design, printmaking and photography. They learn to select and use a variety of materials, tools and techniques, building their confidence and control as they progress through the school. The formal elements of art are woven throughout our learning. Children explore line, shape, colour, form, tone, texture and pattern, learning how these elements can be combined to create different effects and communicate ideas. We place great importance on learning about artists and their work. Pupils encounter artists from different periods, cultures and backgrounds, exploring their ideas, materials, processes and techniques. This develops their understanding of art and provides inspiration for their own work. Children are also encouraged to evaluate and analyse art, using appropriate vocabulary to talk about their own work and the work of others. They learn to reflect on their creative choices, identify strengths, consider improvements and understand that experimentation, mistakes and changes are an important part of the artistic process. Through Art and Design, we aim to nurture creative thinkers, skilled makers and confident young artists who enjoy exploring ideas, expressing themselves and appreciating the world of art.

Computing
At Edward Pauling Primary School, Computing equips children with the knowledge and skills they need to become confident, creative and responsible users of technology. Through a broad and progressive curriculum, pupils learn how digital technology works and how it can be used to solve problems, communicate ideas and create digital content. Children develop their skills across computer science, information technology and digital literacy. They learn about algorithms, programming, coding, sequences, repetition, selection and debugging, developing their ability to think logically and solve problems systematically. Pupils use a range of digital tools to create, edit, organise and present information, including text, images, animations, audio and presentations. Our pupils are encouraged to design, create, test, evaluate and improve their digital projects. They develop an understanding of how data can be collected, represented and interpreted, while learning how computers and networks enable us to communicate and access information. Digital citizenship is an important part of our curriculum. Children learn about online safety, digital footprints, privacy, personal information, respectful communication and responsible use of technology. They are encouraged to make safe and informed choices when using digital devices and the internet. Through Computing, pupils develop computational thinking, creativity, resilience, problem-solving and digital confidence, preparing them to use technology effectively, safely and responsibly both in school and in the wider world.

English
At Edward Pauling Primary School, we aim to provide a high-quality English curriculum, which will develop our children’s skills in reading, writing, speaking, listening and discussion preparing them for a successful life ahead.
*Deliver an engaging and exciting curriculum that helps develop a love of writing and inspires children to want to read and write
*Introduce new learning in manageable steps that builds on current skills and knowledge from previous learning
*Ensure all children have access to a broad English curriculum including a range of book genres
*Explicitly teach new grammar skills and allow children time to embed and apply skills in different contexts
*Create a culture where children love to read and can express their thoughts and ideas clearly and creatively
*Encourage children to read for a range of purposes and encourage a love of reading
At Edward Pauling Primary School, we aim to provide a high-quality reading curriculum starting with the fundamentals of phonics, giving all pupils a strong start to support them in developing a lifelong love of reading. Reading underpins our curriculum and is driven around exposing our children to high-quality texts. We choose our key texts with careful consideration to ensure that books are reflective of our diverse demographics and, that children are engaged and excited by what they read. This is important as we want children to read, not just for purpose, but also for pleasure- ensuring that reading becomes a lifelong habit.

Geography
At Edward Pauling Primary School, Geography encourages children to explore and understand the world in which they live. Through exciting and meaningful learning experiences, pupils develop a sense of place and an understanding of the physical and human processes that shape our planet. Children develop essential geographical skills, including using maps, atlases and globes, locating places, using compass directions, reading and interpreting data, carrying out fieldwork and communicating geographical information. They investigate landscapes, weather, rivers, settlements and environments, while comparing places locally, nationally and around the world. Our pupils are encouraged to ask questions, observe carefully, collect evidence and explain the relationships between people and their environment. They develop an understanding of sustainability, natural resources, climate and environmental change, building the knowledge and skills they need to become informed and responsible citizens who care about the world around them.

History
At Edward Pauling Primary School, History helps children to understand the world around them by exploring the people, places and events that have shaped our past. Through engaging topics and carefully sequenced learning, pupils develop a sense of chronology and an understanding of how Britain and the wider world have changed over time. Children learn to ask questions, investigate evidence, identify change and continuity, make connections and form their own conclusions. They explore a range of historical sources, including artefacts, photographs, documents and accounts, developing the skills needed to consider different perspectives and understand how historians find out about the past. Our curriculum enables pupils to explore significant individuals, civilisations and historical events, while making connections between local, national and global history. Through visits, artefacts, stories and practical experiences, children develop a curiosity about the past, a respect for different cultures and an appreciation of how history continues to influence our lives today.

Design & Technology
At Edward Pauling Primary School, Design and Technology inspires children to become creative, curious and confident designers, makers and problem-solvers. Through practical, hands-on experiences, pupils learn to design, make, evaluate and improve products for real-life purposes and users. Following the Kapow Primary scheme, children develop a broad range of skills across structures, mechanisms and mechanical systems, textiles, cooking and nutrition, electrical systems and the digital world. They learn to explore and select appropriate materials, tools and techniques, develop and communicate design ideas, and make purposeful products with increasing independence. Our pupils develop practical skills such as cutting, joining, shaping, sewing, constructing, strengthening structures, creating and testing mechanisms, preparing and cooking food, investigating electrical circuits and using digital technology to design and solve problems. Children are encouraged to test, evaluate and refine their ideas, learning that designers and engineers use creativity, perseverance and problem-solving to improve their work. Through a progressive curriculum, pupils build on previous knowledge and develop the confidence and technical understanding to design solutions that are functional, innovative and fit for purpose.
